name: Chris Nocco

items.text: A 2020 Tampa Bay Times investigation reported a sheriff's program that sent deputies repeatedly to families' homes, including children's. In a December 2024 settlement, his office acknowledged it interfered with four residents' constitutional rights, ended the program and agreed to pay $105,000. The office said it settled to save taxpayers money and won't apologize.
items.why: Under criterion 6 (abuse of office), the sheriff's own office signed a settlement acknowledging its program he created violated residents' constitutional rights; this is an agency admission, not a court finding, so it takes the nearest level, 3.

for_review: I read the settlement through Florida Phoenix and Reason coverage, not the agreement itself. Reason links it at ij.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/FedEx-Scan-2024-12-04_10-57-01.pdf, but I couldn't open that link. I also didn't open the Tampa Bay Times series itself. The sheriff's office says a court found its written policies constitutional, that it won all earlier cases, and that the Times relied on false reporting by former employees. I didn't verify those claims. The office also said in 2023 that it never engaged in predictive policing, which a reviewer could compare with the settlement. The one search on the owner's named sites (Alex Jones, Stew Peters, Infowars) found nothing about Nocco. The weight of 3 is a judgment call. A reviewer may prefer a lower weight because the admission came in a settlement and no court ruled against him.
